note.text: A declarative normally states information; an interrogative normally asks a question; an imperative can give an instruction or request; an exclamative expresses a strong reaction through its construction. Form and communicative purpose can differ: Could you close the door? is interrogative in form but can function as a polite request. An exclamation mark alone does not turn every sentence into an exclamative structure. Read the grammar and situation, not merely the final sign.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish declarative, interrogative, imperative and exclamative forms without relying on punctuation alone. Builds on: verb and clause patterns in statements and questions. Leads to: argumentative writing and sentence-structure analysis.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: A declarative normally states information; an interrogative normally asks a question; an imperative can give an instruction or request; an exclamative expresses a strong reaction through its construction. Form and communicative purpose can differ: Could you close the door? is interrogative in form but can function as a polite request. An exclamation mark alone does not turn every sentence into an exclamative structure. Read the grammar and situation, not merely the final sign.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original models: Bih has the book. Has Bih brought it? Bring the book, please. What a useful book it is! The imperative normally omits the subject you. A question can also request an action, so identify whether an exercise asks for grammatical form or communicative purpose.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Find the finite verb, subject pattern and any imperative or exclamative construction. Label form and function separately when needed. Use punctuation to support the construction instead of letting it decide everything by itself.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Every declarative must ask a direct question. Correction: This form states information.
A polite request can never use interrogative form. Correction: A question form can function as a request in context.
An imperative always needs you written before the base verb. Correction: The directive model normally leaves you unexpressed.
Any sentence becomes an exclamative structure solely by adding an exclamation mark. Correction: The construction, not just the mark, matters.
